A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Antidistillation Fingerprinting. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original GSM8K and OASST1 experiments, including detection-quality trade-offs, data-mixture experiments, ROC/FPR analyses, and generated examples.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds MBPP experiments and a GSM8K study of alternative student fine-tuning regimes.

M1.justification: The ADFP perturbation, proxy-based sampling, and fingerprint detection procedures remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Algorithms 1–2. The added full fine-tuning and QLoRA variants concern experimental students, not changes to ADFP.

E1.justification: V2 adds MBPP code generation to the retained GSM8K mathematical reasoning and OASST1 dialogue tasks. Function completion introduces a distinct output domain and execution-based correctness requirements, substantially broadening evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Red-and-green-list fingerprinting remains the evaluated competing method, with unfingerprinted controls where applicable. The new experiments retain these comparison roles; the added Ma et al. citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an MBPP protocol using 674 pooled problems, code-specialized checkpoints, three-epoch LoRA training, greedy training-trace generation, stochastic evaluation traces, and execution/syntax utility metrics. Appendix B.2 also adds fixed-trace comparisons of full fine-tuning for one or three epochs and 8-bit/4-bit QLoRA. Existing GSM8K/OASST1 protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 and Table 1 directly test whether ADFP's relative advantage depends on the student's training regime. Comparing original LoRA with full-parameter and quantized adaptation adds a substantive robustness analysis beyond the retained mixture-fraction, ROC/FPR, and qualitative studies.

E5.justification: Both versions already report ten-trial log-space averages with 1.96-times-SEM error bars and 100-trial ROC/FPR analyses. Table 1 extends the existing ten-run log-space uncertainty convention to additional settings; existing run counts and statistical procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds MBPP results showing a favorable unsupervised trade-off but similar supervised trade-offs versus red-and-green-list fingerprinting (Figures 4 and 9). Table 1 adds training-regime results; for three-epoch full fine-tuning, open-weight mean natural-log p-values are -7.914 for ADFP versus -1.064 for the baseline. Original plotted results and qualitative examples are retained.

T1.justification: The GTP definition, hash assumptions, Hoeffding detection bound, perturbation derivation, and isotropic-approximation proposition remain unchanged. Appendix A.1–A.2 retains the same proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion explicitly extend the empirical effectiveness claim to code generation alongside reasoning and dialogue. The central contribution and claimed mechanism remain the same.

C2.justification: The learning-dynamics explanation and qualifications concerning supervised data access, proxy mismatch, and low fingerprinted-data fractions are retained. The new comparisons add empirical observations without substantive new mechanism explanations or limitations arguments.

D1.justification: Sections 5.1 and A.3–A.4 document MBPP checkpoint identifiers, prompt construction, decoding parameters, and training duration, while B.2 specifies the alternative adaptation settings. Hardware, software libraries, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Austin et al. (2021) for MBPP and Ma et al. (2026) on unauthorized-distillation protection through trace rewriting. The broader positioning relative to watermarking, membership inference, and antidistillation sampling is retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized edits integrating MBPP, adds Appendix B.2, and renumbers subsequent appendix subsections. Publication text and the impact-section heading also change, while the main narrative and organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds two four-panel MBPP figures and the fine-tuning comparison table. Existing figures retain their graphical content, with renumbering, relocation, and page reflow; the overall visual design remains consistent.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support by adding code-generation evaluation and testing the relative advantage under full and quantized student fine-tuning. These gains are bounded: supervised MBPP shows similar trade-offs, and the new training-regime study uses one GSM8K perturbation pair. With the original method, proofs, and evidence preserved, this is a useful but limited overall improvement.
